XPT_table2.quote_def: be the cause of death within a 5-year period for more than 10% of humans alive at the beginning of that period
XPT_table2.quote_q7: non-anthropogenic causes (e.g., asteroid or comet impacts, solar flares, a supervolcanic eruption, or a stellar explosion)
XPT_table2.note_pathogen: Engineered and natural pathogen questions asked in a one-shot postmortem survey (N=78 superforecasters, 45 domain experts).

Toba.quote: Modeling on an emission of 8.5e14 g of sulfur, which is 100 times the 1991 Pinatubo sulphur, volcanic winter has a maximum global mean cooling of 3.5 C and returns gradually within the range of natural variability 5 years after the eruption.
Toba.quote2: The Lake Malawi studies suggest that the environmental effects of the eruption were mild and limited to less than a decade in East Africa, but these studies are questioned because of sediment mixing

Xia2022_cooling.quote: the maximum average 2 m air temperature reductions range from 1.5 C (5 Tg soot injection) to 14.8 C (150 Tg soot injection), peaking within 1-2 years after the war, with temperature reduction lasting for more than 10 years.

Impact_event.quote: Asteroids with a 1 km diameter strike Earth every 500,000 years on average. ... Large collisions - with 5 km objects - happen approximately once every twenty million years.

Chapman_Morrison_1994.quote: There is a 1-in-10,000 chance that a large (~2-km diameter) asteroid or comet will collide with the Earth during the next century, disrupting the ecosphere and killing a large fraction of the world's population.

Carrington_Event.quote: In June 2013, a joint venture from researchers at Lloyd's of London and Atmospheric and Environmental Research (AER) in the US used data from the Carrington Event to estimate the cost of a similar event in the present to the US alone at US$600 billion to $2.6 trillion
